page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Memory bandwidth tests show read-only small block speeds of 925.05 GB/sec, large block read speeds of 153.96 GB/sec, and large block write speeds of 86.14 GB/sec. CPU performance is generally average, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core scores falling in the middle 50%. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression represents a relative strength, scoring in the top 25% at 14.33 GB/sec. However, encryption performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%.

The r8gn.2xlarge is designed for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching layers, as demonstrated by its average Redis SET throughput of 17.78 million operations per second and average database operations score. While the instance delivers high memory density and strong memory bandwidth, it is less suited for cryptographic tasks or heavy machine learning inference. LLM inference benchmarks show weak performance for text generation on small models (48.61 tokens/sec) and poor performance for prompt processing on medium 7B models (15.62 tokens/sec). This makes the instance highly efficient for memory-bound applications like Redis caching and relational databases, but less optimal for compute-heavy or AI-driven workloads.
